title: Friday Earnings: Moderna Beats and Raises; Humana Lifts Guidance; Vistra, Oklo, TeraWulf and Charter Report
dek: Six companies on Earnings Whispers' Friday list reported before the open. Moderna and Humana raised full-year outlooks; Charter announced a new operating model and a $2 billion savings plan.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Black-and-white photograph of an automatic ticker apparatus on the New York Stock Exchange trading floor
image.credit: Library of Congress via Wikimedia Commons

keyPoints: Moderna reported Q3 revenue of $1.31 billion, up 29%, and GAAP EPS of 38 cents against an expected loss of $1.25 (CNBC; LSEG consensus). It raised 2026 revenue growth guidance to 15%-25%, from up to 10% (CNBC; company release via Yahoo Finance).
Humana reported Q3 GAAP EPS of $1.33 and raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $9.50, from at least $9.00 (Humana release, Business Wire, Nov. 6).

Vistra reported Q3 GAAP net income of $1,140 million and Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA of $2,378 million, and raised the midpoint of its 2026 EBITDA guidance to a $7.1 billion-$7.5 billion range (Vistra release, PR Newswire).

Oklo reported Q3 sales of $1.86 million and a net loss of $41.75 million (MarketScreener). TeraWulf reported Q3 revenue of $76.2 million, including $63.0 million of HPC lease revenue, and net income of about $709.9 million, helped by a non-cash item (TeraWulf release, GlobeNewswire, Nov. 6).

Charter reported Q3 results alongside a new operating model and a $2 billion annualized expense-savings plan. GAAP net loss per share attributable to Charter shareholders was $20.50 (Charter release, PR Newswire).
body:
## Six reports before the bell

Earnings Whispers listed MRNA, OKLO, VST, WULF, CHTR and HUM as reporting before Friday's open. Each has now published third-quarter results. None of them reported after the close, so the market reaction was already in Friday's session. Earnings Whispers also listed HE and TOMZ after the close; we did not verify those reports and do not cover them here.

## Moderna: a beat and a raise

Moderna reported third-quarter revenue of $1.31 billion, up 29%, with GAAP net income of $162 million, or 38 cents a share. LSEG consensus had called for a loss of $1.25 a share and revenue of $885.1 million, according to CNBC. The company raised its 2026 revenue growth outlook to 15%-25%. Shares rose roughly 3% in premarket trading.

## Humana: guidance up

Humana reported third-quarter GAAP EPS of $1.33 and an adjusted loss of $0.70 a share. Its insurance-segment benefit ratio was 93.7%, better than the 'slightly above 94%' guidance. It raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $9.50 and GAAP EPS guidance to at least $15.09.

## Vistra: power demand

Vistra reported GAAP net income of $1,140 million, which included a $559 million unrealized hedge gain, and Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA of $2,378 million, more than 50% higher than a year earlier. The company closed its Cogentrix acquisition, adding about 5,500 MW of gas-fired generation, and authorized an extra $1.5 billion of buybacks.

## Oklo and TeraWulf: AI-power names

Oklo's Q3 sales were $1.86 million, with a net loss of $41.75 million, according to MarketScreener. Oklo's company release confirmed the results and an 8:30 a.m. ET call. TeraWulf reported Q3 revenue of $76.2 million, of which $63.0 million was high-performance computing lease revenue. Its net income of about $709.9 million reflected a non-cash item, so it should not be read as operating profit.

## Charter: new operating model

Charter reported a net loss of $20.50 a share attributable to shareholders, compared with income of $8.50 a year earlier. It also announced a $2 billion annualized expense-savings plan on top of more than $1 billion of planned synergies from the Cox deal. Management said it will reformulate its go-to-market approach and aims to return to internet customer growth.

## What to watch

The reports are mostly backward-looking, but the guidance changes matter for the next quarter. Vistra and Humana raised outlooks; Moderna did too. Charter's savings plan is a restructuring signal rather than a near-term revenue story.

marketImpact.summary: Guidance changes drove the Friday read-through more than the headline results. Moderna, Humana and Vistra raised outlooks, while Charter's new operating model and savings plan point to a restructuring that could shape its next several quarters.
marketImpact.timeframe: Friday, Nov. 6 pre-market releases, and the following week's earnings slate

Raised the midpoint of 2026 EBITDA guidance and authorized $1.5 billion more buybacks (Vistra release).
Reported a $20.50 GAAP loss per share and announced a restructuring-style operating model (Charter release).
